title: Terminal admission and post-removal completion
purpose: A stopped scheduler can accept work that cannot receive a reply, and an early exit record cannot prove process-table removal. Close these two gaps in beamr so Haematite and liminal can await owned signals. This brief orders implementation and qualification; it does not claim either defect fixed.

requirements.title: Refuse terminal-process admission and settle abandoned work
requirements.spec: WHEN scheduler shutdown has returned or a target process reaches its irreversible terminal boundary, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse enqueue_atom_message with false through its existing surface. WHEN an accepted request races that boundary, THE SYSTEM SHALL execute it before termination or release the scheduler-owned queued request and its reply sender before terminal completion returns. WHILE a waiting, suspended, or executing process remains resumable, THE SYSTEM SHALL preserve admission and wake behavior. THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT add work to the steady live-message path. R1 spawn amendment: reserve the existing teardown admission before direct bytecode process publication and retain the reservation through publication. Refusal returns ExecError::SchedulerTerminated before allocating a pid, inserting a process body/table entry, or recording any tombstone. Shutdown closes admission and waits for racing publishers; a bare shutdown atomic is insufficient. Lead amendment A (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Hermes 2d53fc73 confirmed in 8c7dd37a and Waffles ed1f31bb; source at 05adf473): WHEN scheduler shutdown has returned, THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse send_to_mailbox with the new MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated, at the same admission boundary as enqueue_atom_message, before any copy into the target heap or any wake, and SHALL drop the refused OwnedTerm in the caller's frame so that any reply sender it owns closes. send_to_mailbox and enqueue_atom_message share timer_integration.rs's delivery functions (deliver_owned_term_to_mailbox and deliver_term_to_mailbox, which read exit_tombstones and the slot but never shutdown), so a refusal placed there covers both; a refusal placed only in enqueue_atom_message does not meet this requirement. MailboxSendError carries no #[non_exhaustive] at 05adf473, so the new variant is a breaking change: CHANGELOG records it beside ExecError::SchedulerTerminated, and its Display text is 'scheduler has shut down'. ProcessTerminated keeps its meaning (a retained exit tombstone) and SHALL NOT be reused for a stopped scheduler. Process-to-process sends ('!', send_local, bif_send) keep the BEAM silent drop for an absent pid (native/local_send.rs:21, supervision_integration.rs:941); this requirement governs the host enqueue surface only. Lead amendment C (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Vanilla Slice's audit of R1 at 4dfe833c: R1's joined-shutdown drain finalizes every current process): the refusal variant after shutdown is chosen only on the path that already refuses. Per pid, R1's drain installs the exit record before table removal and the completion watch fires after removal, so a send that reaches a drained pid meets its exit record and is refused before that pid's watch can fire; no new check is added to the live-message path. WHEN admission is closed and the existing check would refuse (exit record present or slot Absent), THE SYSTEM SHALL answer MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated, and enqueue_atom_message SHALL answer false. Before shutdown every existing variant keeps its meaning. A send that admission accepted before the close is executed or released by the drain, as R1 already requires.
acceptance: Behavioral red on published beamr 0.20.0 at 05adf473333ddafdc85691634c14a49d60abc8c0: spawn a native process whose ready channel proves it reached NativeOutcome::Wait; keep scheduler and process handle alive; call scheduler.shutdown and join that owned stop; assert enqueue_atom_message(pid, marker) == false. Published code accepts the retained Present body after its worker has joined. Failure must be this boolean assertion, not an unresolved symbol, compiler error, timeout, or deliberately hung receiver.

Use an embedder-shaped owned command queue whose Shutdown command owns the last reply sender. After the readiness handshake and joined shutdown, queue that command, attempt enqueue, and handle false by dropping the exact command. Assert the reply receiver is disconnected using try_recv and the command was not executed, while queue and scheduler remain alive. List every sender clone; drop deliberate extras before the disconnection assertion. beamr cannot close a sender independently owned by an embedder.

Coordinate accepted-before-close, admission-contending-with-close, and rejected-after-close cases with barriers/channels at the actual admission and finalization boundaries. For each command ID assert exactly one executed reply or explicit rejection/drop, no duplicate execution, no retained scheduler-owned request/completion sender after stop, and executed + dropped == submitted. An abandoned HostOwned mailbox completion settles through the existing typed terminal error. Record observations, release barriers, join workers, and clean up before evaluating a red assertion.

Keep positive cases for ordinary receive, Executing-slot deferred delivery, and result-gated suspension. A parked process is not terminal. Preserve existing bool and MailboxSendError interfaces, OwnedTerm ownership, message order, and shutdown service ownership. A check outside slot ownership must not create a check-then-enqueue race.

Run N=128 and N=256 live-message workloads separately for Present, Executing, and result-gated-suspended targets, with identical worker count, payload, preallocation, and release signals on published baseline and candidate. Count actual map/table probes, slot/wait-set lock acquisitions, lifecycle/admission atomic reads, heap/message allocations, term copies, mailbox pushes, wake calls/notifications, and whole-state clones at call sites. Assert each candidate component per N <= its measured published baseline and delivered == N after resumption. Do not hide a new per-message lifecycle check in an uncounted helper. Report full before/after vectors and N; no counts were measured in this authoring box.

Place any necessary extra work on the one terminal transition under existing admission ownership instead of new per-message polling, callbacks, history scans, or locks. Count cleanup visits/released requests separately; bound them by currently owned processes/queued requests, not all historical pids. Introduce no per-message disk sync or downstream copied runtime.

After joined shutdown, direct bytecode spawning and trap-exit spawning return ExecError::SchedulerTerminated. Observe unchanged next_pid, no new process-table/body entry and no new tombstone. Also rendezvous a publisher holding the existing admission reservation against shutdown: close waits until publication completes, and terminal cleanup leaves no admitting body. The published behavioral red uses the existing spawn surface and records a returned pid/admitting body before cleanup; the new error surface is candidate-only, and a missing symbol or exhaustive-match compiler error is never a red. No minted pid with a Normal tombstone stands in for refusal.

Change enqueue_spawn_with_trap_exit and its two private wrappers to Result<u64, ExecError>, propagating through the existing Result-returning public spawn entrypoints; both test-support scaffolds return Result too. Document SchedulerTerminated in error.rs and its Display mapping. ExecError is exhaustive, so CHANGELOG names the breaking variant and scaffold return change. Caller Result handling and exhaustive matches require their separately owned follow-up, with explicit variant arms rather than a wildcard bypass. Existing bool and MailboxSendError surfaces remain. Add the explicit SchedulerTerminated => scheduler_terminated arm to the exhaustive Wasm reason mapping, preserve every existing label, and name this additive wire-visible reason in CHANGELOG.

Lead amendment A (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Hermes 2d53fc73 confirmed in 8c7dd37a and Waffles ed1f31bb; source at 05adf473): Behavioral red on published 0.20.0: spawn a process that parks in receive, join scheduler shutdown, then send_to_mailbox an owned tagged tuple that owns a reply sender. 0.20.0 answers Ok (the red). The candidate answers Err(MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated), the target mailbox length is unchanged, no wake is recorded, and the reply receiver observes disconnection on a blocking recv once send_to_mailbox has returned, with no timeout in the test.

Lead amendment A (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Hermes 2d53fc73 confirmed in 8c7dd37a and Waffles ed1f31bb; source at 05adf473): With the scheduler running, send_to_mailbox to a live parked process still answers Ok and the receive observes the message; to a tombstoned pid it still answers ProcessTerminated; to an unknown pid NoSuchProcess.

Lead amendment C (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Vanilla Slice's audit of R1 at 4dfe833c: R1's joined-shutdown drain finalizes every current process): after joined shutdown, send_to_mailbox to a drained pid answers Err(MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated), not ProcessTerminated, and to a never-spawned pid also SchedulerTerminated; enqueue_atom_message answers false for both. Live-message observer counts for Present, Executing and result-gated targets equal the published baseline's.

requirements.title: Observe process-table removal without telemetry
requirements.spec: WHEN the winning finalizer removes a process from process_table, THE SYSTEM SHALL offer an additive notification-only one-shot completion watch whose successful answer proves that removal. Registration SHALL answer Live(watch), AlreadyRemoved(pid, reason), or NoRecord. A still-present process with an early exit record SHALL remain Live. Fire SHALL follow successful table removal and release of its map guard, outside telemetry. Existing outcome installation, exclusive exit-event ordering, watch_exit behavior, and exactly-once outcome consumption SHALL remain. Lead amendment A (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Hermes 2d53fc73 confirmed in 8c7dd37a and Waffles ed1f31bb; source at 05adf473): Scheduler::shutdown (execution.rs:70-133 at 05adf473) joins workers without terminating live processes, so a completion watch on a process still present when shutdown returns would otherwise never answer. THE SYSTEM SHALL settle every outstanding completion watch before shutdown returns, by dropping its sender so the receiver observes disconnection, and a disconnection SHALL NOT be read as removal. WHEN completion registration happens after shutdown has returned and the pid was not removed, registration SHALL answer the fourth answer SchedulerStopped(pid), never Live. No answer in this requirement SHALL depend on a timeout. The existing watch_exit ExitWatch keeps its contract here, although it has the same hang for a process live at shutdown (its receiver holds the registry Arc that owns the sender, exit_events.rs:151-156 and :232-246); that hazard is named for a follow-up brief and is not changed by B-179. Lead amendment B (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Apollo's review of 129d655b against the Haematite hang 48655c02, point 3): inside Scheduler::shutdown, THE SYSTEM SHALL close admission (R1: enqueue_atom_message answers false, send_to_mailbox answers MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated, direct spawn answers ExecError::SchedulerTerminated) BEFORE it settles any completion watch. A consumer that drains its own queue when its watch disconnects (Haematite registers watch_exit_completion per shard pid and gives every queued command ActorUnavailable on disconnection) SHALL never see a wake admitted after that drain, because such a command's caller would wait with no further signal. No timeout is used to order the two. Lead amendment C (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Vanilla Slice's audit of R1 at 4dfe833c: R1's joined-shutdown drain finalizes every current process): R1 drains and finalizes every current process when shutdown is joined, so shutdown's order is: close admission (R1), drain and finalize every remaining process, with each completion watch firing on its genuine removal, then settle by disconnection only a watch whose pid the drain did not finalize (counted; 0 expected), then return. Amendment A's premise that a parked process stays present after shutdown holds at published 0.20.0, not under R1, so the registration answer SchedulerStopped(pid) is withdrawn: after shutdown registration answers AlreadyRemoved or NoRecord, and the answer set is Live, AlreadyRemoved and NoRecord as B-179 first wrote it.
acceptance: Behavioral red on published 0.20.0: hold an owned test-only rendezvous after exit-record installation but before process_table.remove. The existing install_event_publication_gate holds publication after its send; use a blocking channel-based test accessor compiled identically for baseline and candidate instead of its timed helper. While held, assert process_table.get(pid).is_some(), register the published watch_exit adapter, and record AlreadyExited. Release, join, and clear the fixture before asserting that an immediate completion answer must imply table absence. Published code fails that assertion because its record precedes removal. A missing proposed API is not a red.

Provide one additive scheduler registration surface (proposed name watch_exit_completion) with typed Live/AlreadyRemoved/NoRecord answers and a one-shot receiver. Arm before checking removal, then recheck with ordering that closes registration-versus-removal and lookup-versus-publication races. A tombstone alone never proves removal. Unknown pid returns NoRecord and retains no watch.

Repeat the held-gap case using completion registration before exit and during the early-record gap: both remain pending while process_table.get(pid) is Some, proven by nonblocking observation at the rendezvous. Release; await the real completion channel; assert exact pid/reason and table absence; join the finalizer. After removal, registration answers AlreadyRemoved immediately. Exercise all three positions and concurrent winning/losing finalizers using signals. No sleeps, clock polling, raised timeouts, skipped assertions, or serial markers.

Existing watch_exit retains its early-record contract and subscribe_exit_events keeps its one-per-scheduler-lifetime stream, outcome-before-event ordering, and Lagged behavior. A completion observer never calls take_exit_outcome or claims the stream. With multiple completion watches, assert the existing outcome owner can still take exactly one outcome. After outcome consumption and bounded tombstone eviction, AlreadyRemoved still reports pid/reason using the existing authoritative retained record; do not create another permanent historical pid ledger.

Only the winning table-removal token fires completion once per watch. Duplicate cleanup, watcher drop, and receiver disconnection retain no slots and run no user callbacks under internal locks. Drop deregisters; fire removes slots; registration counts return to their starting value after every scenario. The guarantee is table absence, not completion of the separately owned resource-release path for an Executing body.

Run completion tests without and with telemetry, and each threaded/cooperative configuration supporting this API. Preserve existing exit-observation, supervision, service ownership, and mailbox assertions. Repeat R1 N=128/256 vectors with 0 and 128 completion watches on unrelated pids: each per-message component stays <= published baseline. Separately count exit-watch lookups/sends, bounded by watches for this pid without scanning all watchers or process history. Report complete vectors; runtime reds/greens/counts are not measured in this authoring box.

Lead amendment B (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Apollo's review of 129d655b against the Haematite hang 48655c02, point 3): hold Scheduler::shutdown at an owned test-only rendezvous after the completion watches have settled and before shutdown returns; observe a watched process's receiver disconnected; then call enqueue_atom_message for that pid and assert false, and send_to_mailbox and assert Err(MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated). The reverse order is the red: a build that settles watches first admits the wake at the rendezvous. This case needs R1 and R2 together and is written in the merge that joins them.

Lead amendment C (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Vanilla Slice's audit of R1 at 4dfe833c: R1's joined-shutdown drain finalizes every current process): supersedes amendment A's shutdown case. Register a completion watch on a process parked in receive, then join shutdown. R1's drain finalizes that process, and the watch answers removal through the winning finalizer with the drain's terminal reason; process_table().get(pid) is None when it answers. Registration after shutdown answers AlreadyRemoved(pid, reason) for that pid and NoRecord for a pid never spawned. The count of watches settled by disconnection in that shutdown is 0. The test holds no timeout.

boundaries: Authoring changes only this hand-written JSON/Markdown pair and seven additions-only B-179 path keys in legacy design.json.structure, under Hermes ruling13479841. Every existing declaration byte stays unchanged; no schema conversion. Requirement file lists describe a later implementation and name existing paths. No production code, public interface, stored shape, Cargo dependency, consumer bump, gate, or other brief is edited now. Story S15 is shared with B-012/NATIVE-003: B-179 delivers only terminal admission and table-removal observation, leaving their existing scope untouched.

Exactly two requirements. The approved R1 exception changes direct spawn admission to the named ExecError::SchedulerTerminated refusal, adds that exhaustive error variant, and changes the two test-support scaffold returns to Result; CHANGELOG records the breaking change. Existing bool/MailboxSendError and event/outcome contracts remain; R2 completion is additive. Stop and refer to the beamr lead for any other changed public interface, wire format, stored shape, shared-service ownership, or broader spawn/restart policy.

Haematite and liminal adopt a qualified published beamr release by version bump only. No vendored/copied runtime, downstream lifecycle wrapper, or timeout workaround. Apollo reviews R1 against the Haematite hang; Hermes reviews R2 against the five liminal sites.

Do not equate scheduler.shutdown with removal of every process or an early exit notification with table removal. Source: execution.rs:126-133 joins workers and :369-370 stops dispatch; timer_integration.rs:154-211 admits from body slots without scheduler-stop checking; core.rs:1643-1646 records exit first, :1682-1686 removes the table entry before telemetry.

Reuse authoritative existing outcome/reason retention. New watches retain live registrations only and remove them on fire/drop. No second permanent pid ledger, history scan, whole-state clone, or per-message disk sync. Existing retained records are source behavior, not new storage here.

Build fixtures once per workload variant outside measured loops. Add phase rendezvous/counters identically under test-only compilation at both pins and verify baseline production bodies unchanged. Release/join every producer before red assertions. A red is the intended behavioral assertion, never compilation failure or a hung nextest run.

Lead amendment A (Artemis, beamr lead, 8 October 2026, from Hermes 2d53fc73 confirmed in 8c7dd37a and Waffles ed1f31bb; source at 05adf473): the beamr lead rules the one further breaking public change, MailboxSendError::SchedulerTerminated, and the additive SchedulerStopped registration answer. Nothing else public changes. watch_exit's shutdown hang is out of scope and named for a follow-up brief.
